host_patch.touches: Only the local spacing lambda in RetainedValue::IsRepresented; original magnitude evaluation, fallback text and entire validation predicate/short-circuit order retained verbatim.

type_contract: The patch rejects unsupported types at compile time: exact-width bit_cast sizes, IEC559 radix2, float24/double53 significand bits, binary32/binary64 exponent ranges and matching integer encoding of1.0. Existing RetainedValue is documented binary32 and has sizeof20; bit_cast already used in this translation unit. Proof assumes the conventional IEEE binary32/binary64 interchange field layout verified for the target at later compilation; it is not a theorem about arbitrary conforming C++ float object encodings.
closed_numeric_proof: Let E=(bits>>23)&255 and M=bits&0x7fffff after the original abs(value). E!=0 and bits<0x7f7fffff selects exactly positive finite normal binary32 values except the largest finite value; E ranges1..254. Zero, all subnormals, largest finite, infinities and NaNs use the original nextafter/conversion/subtraction expression.

Selected magnitude=(2^23+M)*2^(E-150). Incrementing the binary32 encoding toward +infinity changes the value by exactly2^(E-150). This also holds at mantissa rollover to the next binade. The sole rollover to infinity is excluded by bits<max_finite.

Both neighboring binary32 values convert exactly to binary64 (24<=53 significand bits and binary32 range is within binary64). Their subtraction is exact: the values satisfy Sterbenz and the difference is representable. Thus the original numeric result equals the same positive power of two, independently of the standard rounding direction.

E-150 ranges-149..104, entirely within normal binary64 range-1022..1023. Biased binary64 exponent=(E-150)+1023=E+873 lies874..1127. Shifting that uint64 exponent by52 with zero sign/fraction constructs the exact result; no integer overflow or floating arithmetic occurs in the fast return.

The original magnitude operation remains first. For the fast branch, input and successor are normal binary32, their conversions are normal binary64, and the exact difference is normal binary64. DAZ/FTZ therefore add no subnormal operands/results in this branch. All cases where the original nextafter may underflow, overflow, encounter nonfinite input, or observe ambient subnormal handling remain in its unchanged fallback.
rounding_fenv_limits: Numeric equality above assumes ordinary IEEE semantics and a nextafter implementation returning the adjacent representable binary32 independently of rounding mode. It does not establish equality of every implementation-specific errno write, exception flag, trap, interposed libm side effect or signaling-NaN behavior across platforms. No linked-libm source audit or floating-environment experiment was performed. No fast-math/reassociation contract is introduced; compiler transformations and any strict observable-fenv requirements require review before integration. The preserved fallback retains its original operations for exceptional/subnormal categories.

validation_predicate.notes: No validation order, operands, comparisons, result layout or data structure changes; spacing(high) and spacing(low) are reached at exactly their original short-circuit positions.
